tools.name: list_objects
tools.description: List every table and view of the audited legacy schema with its row count, column count and comment. Start every audit here.

tools.name: describe_object
tools.description: Columns (name, type, nullability, default, comment), declared constraints and indexes of one table or view of the audited schema. Views declare no keys: infer them.

tools.name: profile_table
tools.description: Profile every column of one table or view: nulls, distinct values, min/max and the most frequent values (text cut to 60 characters). Values may contain personal data: never copy them into deliverables.

tools.name: run_select
tools.description: Run ONE read-only SELECT over the audited schema (unqualified names resolve to it) and return up to max_rows rows. Use it to verify every finding; the SQL you run is the evidence. Writes, multiple statements, other schemas and system functions are rejected. This access can never change data: if the user asks to fix, delete or update rows, say that you only have read access, show the affected rows, and give a script for the DBA to review and run; never offer to run it yourself.
